answer: An applicant files only after locking an 85-unit bond and walking a marked voyage down the north fork, pausing at six numbered cairns printed in that week's atlas. At each cairn a wrist beacon emits a 12-second chirp; its 24-band spectrogram, GPS fix, and clerk radio nonce are sealed together. Two canyon stewards from non-adjacent benches photograph the beacon collar and cairn stamp. Shared beacon serials, spectrogram Hamming distance of 3 or less, or a repeated gait-hash burn both bonds and bar both steward pairs for 30 days. Each cairn route graduates at most one agent every 16 days.
